region: Indian subcontinent and borderlands (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Sikkim, Himalayan states, North-East, Andaman/Nicobar, Maldives), 1400-1900

polities.name: Delhi Sultanate
polities.note: After Timur's sack (1398) the Tughlaq/Sayyid sultanate held little beyond Delhi and the upper Doab; Bahlul Lodi re-expanded it and annexed Jaunpur (1479); Sikandar Lodi moved the capital to Agra (1506). Ended at Panipat 1526.

polities.name: Mughal Empire
polities.note: Interrupted 1540-1555 by the Sur Empire (Humayun in exile). 1605-1707 phase is the c.1700 maximum; Deccan south of the Kaveri only tributary. After 1707 provinces (Bengal, Awadh, Hyderabad) became autonomous and are listed separately; after 1803 the emperor ruled only the Red Fort under British pension.

polities.name: Sur Empire
polities.note: Sher Shah Suri's empire: Punjab to Bengal, Malwa, much of Rajputana; split among rival Suri claimants after 1553.

polities.name: Jaunpur Sultanate
polities.note: Sharqi sultans; Awadh, eastern Doab and western Bihar. Annexed by Bahlul Lodi 1479.

polities.name: Bengal Sultanate
polities.note: Hussain Shahi phase (1494-1538) held north Bihar and at times Chittagong and Kamata. Sur occupation 1538/39-1553; Karrani sultans (1564-1576) added Orissa (1568). Mughal conquest 1576; Bhati chiefs resisted to 1611.

polities.name: Malwa Sultanate
polities.note: Ghurid then Khalji sultans; Baz Bahadur (1555-1562) last ruler; Mughal conquest 1562.

polities.name: Gujarat Sultanate
polities.note: Kathiawar chiefs (Junagadh after 1472, Nawanagar etc.) tributary; Kutch remained Jadeja. Mughal conquest 1572-73.

polities.name: Khandesh Sultanate
polities.note: Tapti valley; Asirgarh fortress taken by Akbar 1601.

polities.name: Kashmir Sultanate
polities.note: Kashmir valley with Kishtwar/Poonch fringes; under Zain-ul-Abidin (1418-1470) also raided Ladakh and Baltistan. Mirza Haidar Dughlat ruled 1540-1551 nominally for the Mughals.

polities.name: Chak Sultanate of Kashmir
polities.note: Annexed by Akbar 1586; Kashmir then a Mughal subah, Durrani 1752-1819, Sikh 1819-1846, Dogra after 1846.

polities.name: Langah Sultanate
polities.note: Taken by Shah Husain Arghun 1528.

polities.name: Samma Sultanate
polities.note: Lower and middle Sindh; Arghun conquest 1520-1524.

polities.name: Arghun dynasty
polities.note: Expelled from Kandahar by Babur; conquered Sindh and Multan (1528).

polities.name: Tarkhan dynasty
polities.note: Lower Sindh; upper Sindh (Bhakkar) Mughal from 1574; Mughal annexation 1591.

polities.name: Kalhora Sindh
polities.note: Mughal governors who became hereditary rulers of all Sindh; overthrown by the Talpurs at Halani 1783.

polities.name: Talpur Sindh (Hyderabad)
polities.note: Senior Talpur branch (lower and central Sindh, incl. Karachi from 1795). Conquered by Britain at Miani 1843.

polities.name: Khairpur State
polities.note: Upper Sindh Talpur branch; larger before 1843 (incl. Sukkur, Shikarpur fringe), reduced to c.15,700 km2 afterwards.

polities.name: Mirpur Khas Talpurs
polities.note: Third Talpur branch, eastern Sindh toward the Thar; annexed 1843.

polities.name: Khanate of Kalat
polities.note: Confederacy of Brahui and Baloch tribes (Sarawan, Jhalawan) with Kachhi plain; Las Bela, Kharan and Makran were dependencies. Peak under Nasir Khan I (1749-1794).

polities.name: Makran (Kech)
polities.note: Buledi then Gichki chiefs of Kech and Panjgur; Kalat suzerainty from Nasir Khan I. Gwadar was Omani 1783-1958.

polities.name: Bahawalpur
polities.note: Cholistan desert and left bank of the Sutlej/Panjnad.

polities.name: Khanzadas of Mewat
polities.note: Hasan Khan Mewati killed at Khanwa 1527; Mughal province thereafter.

polities.name: Tomaras of Gwalior
polities.note: Gwalior fort taken by Ibrahim Lodi 1523.

polities.name: Durrani Punjab and Kashmir (Afghan provinces)
aliases: Afghan subahs of Lahore, Multan, Kashmir
polities.note: Durrani governors held Multan (to 1818), Kashmir (1752-1819), Peshawar and Derajat; Lahore effectively lost to the Sikh misls by 1765. Use only where misls/Sikh Empire are not drawn. Durrani core is outside this region.

polities.name: Mewar
polities.note: Sisodia Ranas (Guhila house). Peak under Kumbha and Sanga (1433-1528) incl. Ajmer, Ranthambore, Mandalgarh. Chittor fell to Akbar 1568; Udaipur the capital thereafter.

polities.name: Marwar
polities.note: Under direct Mughal occupation 1679-1707. Peak under Maldeo (1532-1562) incl. Nagaur, Ajmer, Jalore, Sambhar.

polities.name: Amber (Jaipur)
polities.note: Shekhawati (north) was a semi-autonomous Kachwaha cadet confederacy, absorbed under Jaipur suzerainty in the 1730s.

polities.name: Shekhawati
polities.note: Rao Shekha's descendants; took Jhunjhunu and Fatehpur from the Kaimkhani nawabs in 1730. Draw under Jaipur after 1738.

polities.name: Bikaner
polities.note: Founded by Rao Bika (Rathore) 1465; Bikaner city 1488.

polities.name: Bundi
polities.note: Kota split off 1631.

polities.name: Kota
polities.note: Jhalawar carved out of it 1838.

polities.name: Sirohi
polities.note: Includes Mount Abu.

polities.name: Dungarpur
polities.note: Senior Guhila branch of Vagad; Banswara split off 1527.

polities.name: Pratapgarh (Deolia)
polities.note: Sisodia cadet line; seat Deolia until Pratapgarh founded 1698.

polities.name: Kishangarh
polities.note: Rathore cadet state of Jodhpur.

polities.name: Alwar
polities.note: Rao Pratap Singh Naruka broke from Jaipur 1770.

polities.name: Bharatpur (Jat state)
polities.note: Under Suraj Mal (1756-1763) held Agra (1761-1774), Mathura, Mewat and parts of the Doab and Haryana.

polities.name: Gohad (Jat Ranas)
polities.note: Held Gwalior fort 1761-1767 and 1780-1784. Moved to Dholpur 1805.

polities.name: Dholpur
polities.note: Granted to the Rana of Gohad in exchange for Gohad.

polities.name: Tonk
polities.note: Scattered: also detached parganas of Nimbahera, Chhabra, Pirawa (Rajputana) and Sironj, Aligarh (Rampura) in Malwa.

polities.name: Jhalawar
polities.note: Separated from Kota 1838 for Zalim Singh's descendants.

polities.name: Cutch
polities.note: Unified by Khengarji I (1548). Extent includes the Rann of Kutch.

polities.name: Nawanagar
polities.note: Jadeja; Mughal occupation as Islamnagar 1664-1709.

polities.name: Chudasama Junagadh
polities.note: Conquered by Mahmud Begada 1472.

polities.name: Bhavnagar
polities.note: Gohil chiefs of Sihor from 13th c.; Bhavnagar founded 1723 and expanded through the 18th c.

polities.name: Porbandar
polities.note: Jethwa seat at Ghumli/Ranpur/Chhaya before Porbandar (1785).

polities.name: Idar
polities.note: Rao dynasty to 1656; Rathores of Jodhpur from 1728; seat moved to Ahmednagar/Himmatnagar 1848.

polities.name: Palanpur
polities.note: Afghan Lohani (Jhalori) dynasty, earlier seated at Jalore; Palanpur from 1682.

polities.name: Dhrangadhra (Halvad)
polities.note: Jhalas of Jhalavad; Wankaner, Limbdi, Wadhwan and Chuda are cadet branches nearby.

polities.name: Gondal
polities.note: Jadeja; Rajkot, Dhrol, Gondal and Morvi are neighbouring Jadeja states.

polities.name: Garha Kingdom
polities.note: Sangram Shah (c.1491-1543) united the '52 garhs' of the upper Narmada; Rani Durgavati defeated by Asaf Khan 1564; northern districts (Chauragarh/Narsinghpur, Sagar side) lost to Mughals and Bundelas. Maratha annexation 1781.

polities.name: Gond Kingdom of Deogarh
polities.note: Founded by Jatba (fl. 1580-1620); Bakht Buland Shah founded Nagpur c.1702. Raghuji I Bhonsle reduced the Gond raja to a pensioner 1743; becomes Nagpur Kingdom.

polities.name: Gond Kingdom of Chanda
polities.note: Wardha-Wainganga basin south to the Godavari (Sirpur). Annexed by Raghuji I Bhonsle of Nagpur 1751.

polities.name: Gond Kingdom of Kherla
polities.note: Betul plateau; Narsingh Rai fought both Malwa and the Bahmanis; annexed by Malwa (treaty with Bahmanis 1467). Later Gond chiefs here were under Deogarh.

polities.name: Bastar
polities.note: Forest kingdom founded by Annam Deo, a Kakatiya refugee from Warangal.

polities.name: Kalachuris of Ratanpur
polities.note: Chhattisgarh '36 forts'; Raipur cadet line from c.1400. Annexed by Bhaskar Pant for the Nagpur Bhonsles 1741 (puppet raja to 1758).

polities.name: Orchha
polities.note: Peak under Bir Singh Deo (1605-1627); Datia split off 1626.

polities.name: Bundela Kingdom of Panna
polities.note: Chhatrasal's Bundela state; on his death (1731) a third went to Peshwa Bajirao I and the rest split into Panna, Jaitpur, Ajaigarh, Charkhari, Bijawar, etc.

polities.name: Bhopal
polities.note: Founded by Dost Mohammad Khan; Hyderabad Nizam briefly asserted control 1720s.

polities.name: Gwalior (Scindia)
polities.note: Under Mahadji Scindia (1768-1794) controlled Delhi and the Doab (to 1803). Lands interlaced with Holkar's; Gwalior fort held from 1780s/1844.

polities.name: Indore (Holkar)
polities.note: Also the detached Rampura-Bhanpura tract (c.24.5N 75.5E) and lands in Khandesh/Deccan before 1818.

polities.name: Jhansi
polities.note: Peshwa's subahdars, hereditary rajas from 1804/1817; annexed by lapse 1853; Rani Lakshmibai held it 1857-58.

polities.name: Nagpur Kingdom (Bhonsle)
polities.note: Absorbed Deogarh, Chanda and Chhattisgarh; held Orissa (Cuttack) 1751-1803 and a share of Berar. Annexed by lapse 1853.

polities.name: Nagvanshis of Chotanagpur
polities.note: Ranchi plateau; reduced to a zamindari under the British. Neighbouring Ramgarh Raj (Hazaribagh) not itemised.

polities.name: Ujjainiya Bhojpur
polities.note: Bhojpuri Rajput chiefs (Dumraon, Jagdishpur); Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur led the 1857 rising.

polities.name: Baglana
polities.note: Rathore (Baharji) hill kingdom between Gujarat, Khandesh and Ahmadnagar; annexed by Aurangzeb 1638.

polities.name: Eastern Ganga dynasty
polities.note: Declining by 1400; last ruler Bhanudeva IV overthrown by Kapilendra Deva 1434.

polities.name: Gajapati Kingdom
polities.note: Kapilendra Deva briefly reached the Kaveri (1460s); Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara pushed the frontier back to the Godavari/Simhachalam 1513-1519.

polities.name: Bhoi dynasty
polities.note: Govinda Vidyadhara's dynasty, then Mukunda Deva (1559-1568), last independent king of Odisha; Karrani conquest 1568.

polities.name: Khurda Kingdom
polities.note: Ramachandra Deva I; custodians of Jagannath; annexed by the British after the 1804 rising (Paika rebellion 1817).

polities.name: Sambalpur
polities.note: Head of the 18 garhjat chiefdoms (Atharagarh); annexed by lapse 1849 (Surendra Sai's revolt 1857-62).

polities.name: Patna State (Patnagarh)
polities.note: Senior Chauhan house, head of the Athara-garh before Sambalpur; capital Bolangir from 1871.

polities.name: Jeypore (Nandapur)
polities.note: Koraput hill country; Silavamsa kings at Nandapur, then Vishwanath Dev's Suryavamshi line (1443/1550s).

polities.name: Paralakhemundi
polities.note: Eastern Ganga cadet line in the Ganjam hills.

polities.name: Vizianagaram
polities.note: Largest Northern Circars zamindari; defeated rival Bobbili 1757.

polities.name: Bengal Subah (Nawabs of Bengal)
polities.note: Murshid Quli Khan to Siraj ud-Daulah (Plassey 1757); Diwani to the Company 1765; nizamat absorbed 1772 (titular nawabs to 1880). Orissa south of Subarnarekha lost to Nagpur 1751.

polities.name: Awadh
polities.note: Benares ceded to the Company 1775; Rohilkhand held 1774-1801; Rohilkhand and the lower Doab ceded 1801. Kingdom from 1819; annexed 1856.

polities.name: Rohilkhand
polities.note: Afghan Rohilla chiefs under Ali Muhammad Khan and Hafiz Rahmat Khan; Najib ud-Daula held Saharanpur/Najibabad separately (to 1770s). Conquered by Awadh with Company troops 1774.

polities.name: Farrukhabad (Bangash)
polities.note: Muhammad Khan Bangash; ceded to the Company 1802.

polities.name: Benares State
polities.note: Balwant Singh's zamindari-kingdom (Benares, Jaunpur, Ghazipur, Mirzapur); Chait Singh revolt 1781; Permanent Settlement 1794 left only the family domains.

polities.name: Oiniwar Tirhut
polities.note: Brahmin dynasty of Mithila; afterwards Mughal Tirhut sarkar with the Khandavala (Raj Darbhanga) family as zamindars from 1557.

polities.name: Mallabhum
polities.note: Bankura region; Maratha raids 1742-51; estate auctioned 1806.

polities.name: Kamata Kingdom (Khen)
polities.note: Conquered by Alauddin Husain Shah of Bengal 1498; Koch rise 1515.

polities.name: Koch Bihar
polities.note: Biswa Singha founded; Nara Narayan and Chilarai (1550s-1580s) briefly dominated Assam, Manipur, Jaintia, Tripura. Split 1581 (Koch Hajo east of the Sankosh).

polities.name: Koch Hajo
polities.note: Raghudev and Parikshit Narayan; Mughal conquest 1612-1616. Remnant Darrang Koch rajas under the Ahoms 1616-1826.

polities.name: Ahom Kingdom
polities.note: Annexed Chutia (1523) and parts of Dimasa land (1536); fought Mughals for Kamrup (border at Manas from 1682, Saraighat 1671). Moamoria rebellion 1769-1805. Upper Assam restored under Purandar Singha 1833-1838 as a British protectorate.

polities.name: Chutia Kingdom
polities.note: Absorbed by the Ahom kingdom 1523-24.

polities.name: Dimasa Kingdom
polities.note: Cachar plains annexed 1832; Tularam Senapati's hill remnant (North Cachar) to 1854.

polities.name: Jaintia Kingdom
polities.note: Syiem Sutnga kings; winter capital Jaintiapur in the plains, summer seat Nartiang in the hills; at times held much of north Sylhet. Annexed 15 March 1835.

polities.name: Khasi Hill States
polities.note: About 25 independent chiefdoms (syiemships) such as Khyrim, Mylliem, Sohra, Nongkhlaw; Anglo-Khasi War 1829-1833.

polities.name: Manipur Kingdom
polities.note: Kabaw valley held at times until 1834; Pamheiba (Garib Niwaz, 1709-1748) raided deep into Burma.

polities.name: Tripura Kingdom

overlord.name: British (plains zamindari of Chakla Roshnabad; hill state protected)

polities.note: Dhanya Manikya and Vijaya Manikya (c.1490-1570) took Chittagong and parts of Sylhet and Noakhali; Mughals annexed the plains (Chakla Roshnabad) 1733.

polities.name: Bhati (Baro-Bhuyans)
polities.note: Confederacy of Bengal landlords led by Isa Khan (d. 1599) and Musa Khan resisting the Mughals in the eastern delta; submitted to Islam Khan 1611. Pratapaditya (Jessore), Kedar Rai (Bikrampur) and the Bhulua/Bakla chiefs were other bhuyans.

polities.name: Chakma Circle
polities.note: Chittagong Hill Tracts; seat Rajanagar (Rangunia) until moved to Rangamati 1874. Bohmong (Marma) and Mong chiefs hold the south and north-west.

polities.name: Naga tribes
polities.note: Village republics and chiefdoms (Konyak angs) with no overall ruler; British Naga Hills district from 1866, Kohima 1878; eastern Naga areas unadministered.

polities.name: Lushai and Kuki chiefdoms
polities.note: Sailo and other Lushai chiefs ruling hill villages; Lushai Hills annexed 1889-1891. Before c.1700 the area was held by earlier Kuki-Chin clans migrating from the Chin hills.

polities.name: Garo tribes
polities.note: Garo Hills; British district 1866-1873.

polities.name: Adi (Abor) tribes
polities.note: Siang valley; independent until the Abor expedition 1911-12.

polities.name: Nyishi and Apatani tribes
polities.note: Subansiri hills north of Assam; Ahom paid posa to hill tribes in return for peace.

polities.name: Bahmani Sultanate
polities.note: Mahmud Gawan added the Konkan (Goa 1472) and coastal Andhra; split into five successor sultanates 1490-1518, sultans puppets of the Barid Shahis until 1527.

polities.name: Bijapur Sultanate
polities.note: Goa lost to the Portuguese 1510; after 1636 conquered 'Karnataka Bijapur' (Bangalore, Kolar, Vellore, Gingee) where Shahaji held jagirs. Western Ghats lost to Shivaji from 1650s. Mughal conquest 1686.

polities.name: Ahmadnagar Sultanate
polities.note: Annexed Berar 1574; Ahmadnagar fort taken by Akbar 1600; Malik Ambar sustained the state from Khadki until 1626; extinguished 1636.

polities.name: Golconda Sultanate
polities.note: Telangana and coastal Andhra; Carnatic gains under Mir Jumla (1640s-50s) south to Cuddapah/Nellore; Mughal conquest 1687.

polities.name: Bidar Sultanate
polities.note: Annexed by Bijapur 1619.

polities.name: Berar Sultanate
polities.note: Annexed by Ahmadnagar 1574.

polities.name: Hyderabad State
polities.note: Northern Circars ceded to the Company 1766-68 and the Ceded Districts (Bellary, Cuddapah) 1800; Berar assigned to Britain 1853. Lost much land to the Marathas 1760-1795.

polities.name: Maratha Empire
polities.note: Extent = lands held directly by the Chhatrapati/Peshwa (Desh, Konkan, Khandesh). The great Maratha chiefs (Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad, Bhonsle of Nagpur, Puars) are listed separately, as are Kolhapur and Thanjavur. Peshwa also held Sagar/Bundelkhand tracts. Ended 1818 (Third Anglo-Maratha War). 1689-1698 Rajaram held court in exile at Gingee in the Carnatic while the homeland was largely occupied by the Mughals.

polities.name: Baroda (Gaekwad)
polities.note: Highly fragmented: Kadi (north), Baroda (centre), Navsari (south) and Amreli/Okhamandal (Kathiawar) prants; Kathiawar chiefs paid it tribute.

polities.name: Kolhapur
polities.note: Tarabai's line; treaty of Warna 1731 fixed it as a separate state.

polities.name: Satara State
polities.note: Restored by the British for Pratap Singh; annexed by lapse 1848. Before 1818 the Satara Chhatrapati was nominal head of the Maratha Empire.

polities.name: Janjira
polities.note: Habshi (Siddi) island fortress never taken by the Marathas; Jafrabad in Kathiawar a dependency.

polities.name: Angres of Kolaba
polities.note: Hereditary Maratha admirals; southern Konkan (Vijaydurg) lost 1756 to the Peshwa and the Company; Kolaba lapsed 1840.

polities.name: Kurnool Nawabs
polities.note: Pathan nawabs; annexed 1839.

polities.name: Cuddapah Nawabs
polities.note: Conquered by Hyder Ali 1779-80.

polities.name: Savanur
polities.note: Larger before 1756 (Bankapur, Hubli, Dharwar districts).

polities.name: Reddi Kingdom
polities.note: Kondavidu fell to Vijayanagara 1424; Rajahmundry branch absorbed by the Gajapatis c.1448.

polities.name: Recherla Velamas
polities.note: Two branches, Rachakonda and Devarakonda (16.69,78.92); allied with the Bahmanis against Vijayanagara; annexed by the Bahmanis c.1475.

polities.name: Portuguese India
polities.note: Goa from 1510 (Velhas Conquistas incl. Bardez/Salcete 1543; Novas Conquistas 1763-1788). Other enclaves: Daman (1559), Diu (1535), Bassein-Chaul 'Province of the North' (1534-1739), Cochin (1503-1663), Nagapattinam, Mylapore, Hooghly (to 1632). Ceylon and Chittagong settlements listed separately or omitted.

polities.name: Portuguese Province of the North
polities.note: Coastal strip from Daman to Chaul incl. Salsette and Bombay (ceded to England 1661); lost to the Marathas 1739 except Daman.

polities.name: French India
polities.note: Pondicherry, Karaikal, Yanam, Mahe, Chandernagore; under Dupleix (1749-1754) dominated the Carnatic and the Northern Circars (Bussy) through client nawabs. Repeatedly occupied by Britain (1761-65, 1778-85, 1793-1816).

polities.name: Danish India
polities.note: Tranquebar (1620-1845) and Serampore (1755-1845); sold to Britain 1845. Nicobar claims 1756-1868.

polities.name: Dutch Coromandel
polities.note: Trading forts with small territory: Pulicat, Nagapattinam, Sadras, Bimlipatnam, and Chinsura (Bengal). Ceded to Britain by 1825.

polities.name: Dutch Malabar
polities.note: Cochin, Quilon, Cranganore and Cannanore forts taken from the Portuguese 1661-63; protector of the Cochin raja. Sold Cannanore to Arakkal 1772; Cochin taken by Britain 1795.

polities.name: East India Company and British Raj
polities.note: Very coarse: only the largest contiguous block per phase (Bengal Presidency and the North-Western Provinces). Madras Presidency (Northern Circars 1766, Carnatic/Ceded Districts 1792-1801, Malabar 1792) and Bombay Presidency (Bombay 1668, Surat 1800, Deccan/Konkan 1818, Sindh 1843) must be taken from the base dataset. After 1858 the Crown is paramount over all princely states, which should be drawn on top.

polities.name: Vijayanagara Empire
polities.note: Kerala lay outside direct rule (Venad tributary at times). After Talikota (1565) the Aravidu rump held the southern Andhra/northern Tamil plains; the nayaks of Madurai, Thanjavur, Gingee, Keladi and Mysore became effectively independent. Bijapur/Golconda took Vellore and Chandragiri 1646.

polities.name: Madurai Nayak dynasty
polities.note: Includes Tirunelveli (palayakkarar chiefs) and Ramnad (Sethupathi) as subordinates; Rani Mangammal regent 1689-1704. Chanda Sahib seized Trichy 1736.

polities.name: Thanjavur Nayak kingdom
polities.note: Kaveri delta; overthrown by Madurai 1673.

polities.name: Thanjavur Maratha kingdom
polities.note: Founded by Venkoji (Ekoji), Shivaji's half-brother; territory ceded to the Company 1799, raja kept Thanjavur fort until lapse 1855.

polities.name: Gingee Nayaks
polities.note: Taken by Bijapur 1649; Maratha (Shivaji) 1677, Rajaram's capital 1689-1698, Mughal 1698.

polities.name: Keladi Nayaka kingdom
polities.note: Malnad and the Canara coast (Tulu Nadu after Shivappa Nayaka, 1645-1660); conquered by Hyder Ali 1763.

polities.name: Kingdom of Mysore
aliases: Sultanate of Mysore (Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan)
polities.note: Under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan (1761-1799) included Bednur/Canara, Malabar (to 1792), Sira, Bellary/Gooty and Dindigul; Third Anglo-Mysore War (1792) cost half its territory.

polities.name: Chitradurga Nayakas
polities.note: Conquered by Hyder Ali 1779.

polities.name: Kodagu (Haleri)
polities.note: Annexed by the British 1834.

polities.name: Yelahanka Nadaprabhus
polities.note: Bangalore fort lost to Bijapur 1638; Magadi annexed by Mysore 1728.

polities.name: Saluvas of Gersoppa
polities.note: Jain chiefs of the Sharavathi valley and Honnavar coast; Queen Chennabhairadevi (1552-1606) traded pepper with the Portuguese; absorbed by Keladi 1606.

polities.name: Sonda (Swadi)
polities.note: Uttara Kannada uplands; conquered by Hyder Ali 1763-64.

polities.name: Tulu Nadu chiefdoms
polities.note: Jain/Bunt chiefs (Chowta, Banga, Ajila, Bhairarasa) of the coastal Tulu country; Rani Abbakka of Ullal resisted the Portuguese (1550s-1570s). Portuguese forts at Mangalore, Barkur, Basrur.

polities.name: Ramnad (Sethupathi)
polities.note: Sivaganga split off c.1725/1730; zamindari estate after 1795/1803.

polities.name: Sivaganga
polities.note: Velu Nachiyar recovered it 1780; Marudu Pandiyar rebellion crushed 1801, zamindari thereafter.

polities.name: Carnatic Sultanate (Nawabs of Arcot)
polities.note: Mughal faujdars turned hereditary nawabs (Navayat, then Wallajah from 1749); Carnatic Wars 1746-1763; territory annexed by the Company 1801, titular nawabs to 1855. Thanjavur, Pudukkottai and Mysore excluded.

polities.name: Palayakkarars of Tirunelveli
polities.note: Dozens of hereditary fort-holding chiefs (eastern Telugu Nayak and western Maravar blocs); Polygar Wars 1799-1801. Similar palayams covered Madurai, Dindigul and the Kongu country.

polities.name: Zamorin of Calicut
polities.note: Leading Malabar sea-trade state; dominated Valluvanad, Tanur and at times Cochin (to 1503 and 1750s). Hyder Ali conquest 1766; British Malabar 1792.

polities.name: Venad and Travancore
polities.note: Marthanda Varma (1729-1758) created Travancore by annexing Attingal, Desinganad, Kayamkulam, Thekkumkur, Vadakkumkur, Chempakassery, etc.; defeated the Dutch at Colachel 1741.

polities.name: Kolathunadu
polities.note: North Malabar from the Chandragiri river (at times the Netravati) to the Korapuzha; Kottayam, Kadathanadu and Arakkal were offshoots/vassals. Ceded 1792, last raja ceded rights 1801.

polities.name: Arakkal Kingdom
polities.note: Only Muslim ruling house of Kerala; held Cannanore town (bought from the Dutch 1772) and the northern Laccadive islands (Amindivi group lost to Tipu 1787; remaining islands sequestered 1875, ceded 1905).

polities.name: Kayamkulam
polities.note: Annexed by Travancore 1746.

polities.name: Thekkumkur
polities.note: Annexed by Travancore 1750.

polities.name: Vadakkumkur
polities.note: Annexed by Travancore 1750.

polities.name: Chempakassery
polities.note: Annexed by Travancore 1754.

polities.name: Palakkad Rajas
polities.note: Absorbed by Mysore 1766.

polities.name: Valluvanad
polities.note: Progressively reduced by the Zamorin; Mysore conquest 1766.

polities.name: Kottayam (Malabar)
polities.note: Included Wayanad; Pazhassi Raja's revolt ended with his death 1805.

polities.name: Sikh Empire
polities.note: Multan 1818, Kashmir 1819, Derajat 1821, Peshawar 1823/1834; Jammu (Gulab Singh) a feudatory and Ladakh conquered by him 1834-42. Annexed by Britain 1849.

polities.name: Bhangi Misl
polities.note: Most powerful misl 1765-1799: Lahore, Amritsar, Gujrat, Sialkot, Chiniot, Jhang (also Multan 1772-1780). Lahore taken by Ranjit Singh 1799.

polities.name: Sukerchakia Misl
polities.note: Ranjit Singh's misl; became the Sikh Empire 1799.

polities.name: Kanhaiya Misl
polities.note: Gurdaspur, Batala, Mukerian, Pathankot; absorbed by Ranjit Singh by 1811.

polities.name: Ramgarhia Misl
polities.note: Jassa Singh Ramgarhia; annexed 1816.

polities.name: Ahluwalia Misl and Kapurthala
polities.note: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, leader of the Dal Khalsa; Kapurthala the seat from 1780.

polities.name: Singhpuria Misl
polities.note: Nawab Kapur Singh's misl; Jalandhar Doab lands annexed by Ranjit Singh, cis-Sutlej lands (Kharar, Manauli) under British protection.

polities.name: Patiala
polities.note: Ala Singh of the Phulkian house; largest cis-Sutlej state.

polities.name: Nabha
polities.note: Phulkian state; detached enclaves (Bawal) not shown.

polities.name: Jind
polities.note: Phulkian state; Sangrur enclave (30.25N 75.85E) also part.

polities.name: Malerkotla
polities.note: Afghan Sherwani nawabs (state from 1657).

polities.name: Kangra (Katoch)
polities.note: Sansar Chand (1775-1823) dominated the hill states until the Gurkha siege (1806-09); fort ceded to Ranjit Singh 1809.

polities.name: Kullu
polities.note: Expanded under Jagat Singh (1637-1672) into Lahaul and Bashahr borderlands; annexed by the Sikhs 1840, British 1846.

polities.name: Sirmur
polities.note: Capital Nahan from 1621.

polities.name: Bashahr
polities.note: Upper Sutlej including Kinnaur; traded with Tibet. Many small 'Simla Hill States' (Keonthal, Jubbal, Baghal, Hindur/Nalagarh) surround it.

polities.name: Guler
polities.note: Katoch cadet branch; famous for Pahari painting.

polities.name: Jammu (Jamwal Raj)
polities.note: Ranjit Dev (1733-1782) made Jammu the leading hill state; annexed by the Sikhs 1808 and re-granted to Gulab Singh as Raja 1822. Many Dogra/Pahari chiefdoms (Basohli, Bhadrawah, Kishtwar, Rajouri, Poonch) not itemised.

polities.name: Jammu and Kashmir
polities.note: Created by the Treaty of Amritsar 1846 for Gulab Singh; includes Ladakh and Baltistan; Gilgit and the Hunza/Nagar tributaries brought under control 1860-1891.

polities.name: Ladakh (Namgyal dynasty)
polities.note: Sengge Namgyal (r. c.1616-1642) conquered Guge and Spiti; Tibet-Ladakh-Mughal war 1679-1684 lost western Tibet. Conquered by Zorawar Singh for the Dogras 1834-1842.

polities.name: Baltistan (Maqpon of Skardu)
polities.note: Ali Sher Khan Anchan (c.1580-1624) briefly ruled Gilgit, Chitral and Ladakh. Shigar (Amacha) and Khaplu (Yabgo) were semi-independent chiefdoms. Dogra conquest 1840.

polities.name: Gilgit (Trakhan dynasty)
polities.note: Rulers of Gilgit and Punial; later disputes among Yasin (Khushwaqt), Nagar and Hunza; Sikh/Dogra occupation from 1842, Kashmir control 1860.

polities.name: Chitral

overlord.name: Jammu and Kashmir / British (nominal then Agency)

polities.note: Khushwaqt branch ruled Upper Chitral and Yasin/Mastuj separately in the 18th-19th c.

polities.name: Yusufzai tribes (Swat, Buner, Mardan)
polities.note: Pashtun tribal confederation in Peshawar valley hills; Akhund of Swat ruled Swat 1849-1878; Dir nawabs from the 1600s/1800s.

polities.name: Afridi and Khyber tribes
polities.note: Autonomous Pashtun tribes of the Khyber and Tirah; never under direct Mughal, Durrani, Sikh or British administration.

polities.name: Waziri and Mahsud tribes
polities.note: Waziristan hills between Kurram and Gomal; independent tribal country.

polities.name: Baloch chiefdoms of the Derajat
aliases: Hot Baloch of Dera Ismail Khan
polities.note: Mirrani chiefs at Dera Ghazi Khan and Hot chiefs at Dera Ismail Khan (31.83N 70.90E); Durrani governors replaced them late 18th c.; Sikh conquest 1819-1821.

polities.name: Garhwal Kingdom
polities.note: Ajay Pal united the 52 garhs (c.1500); Dehradun held to 1803 (Rohilla raids 1757-1770). Gorkha conquest 1803.

polities.name: Tehri Garhwal
polities.note: Western Garhwal restored to Sudarshan Shah after the Anglo-Nepalese War; eastern Garhwal British.

polities.name: Kumaon Kingdom
polities.note: Chand rajas absorbed the Katyuri remnants and the Terai (Tarai/Bhabar) by c.1600; Gorkha conquest 1790-91, British 1815.

polities.name: Malla Nepal (unified)
polities.note: Kathmandu valley kingdom; partitioned after Yaksha Malla (d. 1482).

polities.name: Kantipur
polities.note: Held Nuwakot and routes to Tibet (Kuti) until the Gorkha advance from 1744; Kathmandu fell 1768.

polities.name: Lalitpur (Patan)
polities.note: Fell to Gorkha 1768.

polities.name: Bhaktapur
polities.note: Eastern valley and hills toward Dolakha; fell to Gorkha 1769.

polities.name: Gorkha Kingdom
polities.note: Shah dynasty; Prithvi Narayan Shah took Nuwakot 1744, Makwanpur 1762, the valley 1768-69 - becomes the Kingdom of Nepal.

polities.name: Kingdom of Nepal
polities.note: Absorbed the Chaubisi and Baisi rajyas, Limbuwan and Vijayapur (1774-1790), Kumaon (1791), Garhwal (1803) and hill states to the Sutlej; Treaty of Sugauli 1816 fixed the Kali-Mechi frontier. Western Terai restored 1860.

polities.name: Jumla Kingdom
polities.note: After the Khasa Malla empire broke up (late 14th c.) Jumla led the Baise (22) rajyas of the Karnali; others (Bajhang, Achham, Dailekh, Salyan, Jajarkot, Dullu) not itemised. Gorkha conquest 1789.

polities.name: Doti
polities.note: Katyuri offshoot in the far west of Nepal; fought Kumaon; Gorkha conquest 1790.

polities.name: Palpa
polities.note: Most powerful Chaubisi state under Mukunda Sen (16th c.), with Butwal Terai; annexed by Nepal 1806.

polities.name: Makwanpur
polities.note: Gorkha conquest 1762.

polities.name: Vijayapur (Morang)
polities.note: Eastern Terai Sen kingdom; Limbu chiefs nominally under it; Gorkha conquest 1774.

polities.name: Limbuwan
polities.note: Ten Limbu chiefdoms east of the Arun; joined Nepal by the 1774 treaty retaining kipat autonomy. Khambuwan (Majh Kirat) chiefs between Dudh Kosi and Arun not itemised.

polities.name: Lamjung
polities.note: Chaubisi rajya, Shah dynasty's parent house; annexed 1782.

polities.name: Tanahun
polities.note: Sen-ruled Chaubisi rajya; annexed 1782.

polities.name: Parbat (Malebum)
polities.note: Largest western Chaubisi rajya (Myagdi, Baglung, Parbat); annexed 1786.

polities.name: Kaski
polities.note: Chaubisi rajya around Pokhara; annexed 1781.

polities.name: Sikkim
polities.note: Lost Limbuwan west of the Singalila to Nepal (1780s), Darjeeling to Britain 1835, Morang/Terai 1850.

polities.name: Bhutan
polities.note: Unified by Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal (1616-1651). Held the Bengal and Assam Duars until the Duar War (Treaty of Sinchula 1865) and Kalimpong until 1865. Wangchuck monarchy from 1907 continues the same state.

polities.name: Kingdom of Kotte
polities.note: Parakramabahu VI (1412-1467) unified the island incl. Jaffna 1450-1467; partition of 1521 (Vijayabahu's Spoliation) created Sitawaka and Raigama; Dharmapala bequeathed Kotte to Portugal 1580 (effective 1597).

polities.name: Kingdom of Sitawaka
polities.note: Mayadunne and Rajasinghe I; absorbed Raigama (1538) and Kandy (1582); collapsed after 1593.

polities.name: Kingdom of Raigama
polities.note: Absorbed by Sitawaka 1538.

polities.name: Kingdom of Kandy
polities.note: Highland kingdom; held the east coast (Batticaloa, Trincomalee) intermittently until the Dutch treaty of 1766 left it landlocked. Nayak dynasty from 1739. Ceded to Britain (Kandyan Convention) 1815.

polities.name: Jaffna Kingdom
polities.note: Jaffna peninsula and Mannar; Vanni chiefs tributary. Annexed by Portugal 1619.

polities.name: Vanni chieftaincies
polities.note: Buffer chiefdoms between Jaffna and the Sinhalese kingdoms (Panankamam, Mulliyavalai, Karunavalpattu, Tennamaravadi, Trincomalee, Batticaloa vannimai). Pandara Vanniyan's last resistance 1803.

polities.name: Portuguese Ceylon
polities.note: Kotte lowlands from 1597, Jaffna from 1619; lost to the Dutch 1638-1658.

polities.name: Dutch Ceylon
polities.note: Coastal ring around Kandy (draw Kandy and Vanni on top); full coastline after the 1766 treaty. Galle/Negombo 1640, Colombo 1656, Jaffna 1658. Also protector of the Maldives. Taken by Britain 1796.

polities.name: British Ceylon
polities.note: Coastal provinces 1796-1815 (Kandy separate); whole island after 1815.

polities.name: Maldives Sultanate
polities.note: Atoll chain; Minicoy belonged to the Arakkal/Laccadives side. Malabar raids (Ali Rajas) occupied Male briefly 1752-1753.

polities.name: Great Andamanese tribes
polities.note: Ten tribes in North, Middle and South Andaman; British penal settlement at Port Blair from 1858 (also 1789-1796) devastated them.

polities.name: Jarawa
polities.note: Hostile to outsiders; territory shifted westward in the 19th century as Great Andamanese declined. Overlaps the Great Andamanese polygon.

polities.name: Nicobarese and Shompen
polities.note: Village communities without paramount chiefs; Shompen in interior Great Nicobar.

gaps.area: Thar desert interior (western Rajasthan / Cholistan border)
gaps.note: Not empty but thinly held: claimed by Jaisalmer, Marwar, Bikaner and Bahawalpur; the extents already reach into it. Truly unadministered sand only in patches.
Seasonal salt marsh; nominally Cutch. No settled polity.

gaps.area: Gondwana and Bastar/Abujhmarh forest belt (Amarkantak-Maikal hills, Abujhmarh, Kalahandi/Koraput uplands)
gaps.note: Many small Gond, Bhil, Kol and Khond chiefdoms (e.g. Kanker, Kawardha, Khairagarh, Saraguja, Udaipur-Chhattisgarh, Khondmals) not itemised; the larger Gond kingdoms and Bastar/Kalahandi/Jeypore cover most of it. Khond hills (Ganjam/Phulbani interior) were effectively independent tribal country until c.1850.

gaps.area: Odisha Garhjats (Gangpur, Bonai, Bamra, Rairakhol, Sonepur, Baudh, Dhenkanal, Angul, Talcher, Nayagarh, Ranpur)
gaps.note: Around 26 small hill states between Sambalpur, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj and Khurda; not itemised. Fill with Sambalpur/Patna to the west and Khurda/Keonjhar to the east, or show as fragmented chiefdoms.

Some 200 talukas and thanas (Rajkot, Dhrol, Wankaner, Limbdi, Wadhwan, Jasdan, Jafrabad, Palitana, Okhamandal etc.) between the itemised states; under Gujarat Sultanate, Mughal, Maratha/Gaekwad and British overlordship in turn.

Charkhari, Ajaigarh, Bijawar, Chhatarpur, Samthar, Baoni; Ratlam, Sitamau, Sailana, Jaora, Narsinghgarh, Rajgarh, Khilchipur; Barwani, Ali Rajpur, Jhabua (Bhil country). Not itemised; fill with Panna/Orchha and Gwalior/Indore/Dhar respectively.

gaps.area: Simla Hill States and minor Punjab hill states
gaps.note: Keonthal, Jubbal, Baghal, Baghat, Hindur (Nalagarh), Kutlehr, Jaswan, Datarpur, Siba, Basohli, Bhadrawah, Kishtwar, Rajouri, Poonch; small Rajput chiefdoms between the itemised hill states.

gaps.area: Nepal: remaining Baisi and Chaubisi rajyas, Khambuwan
gaps.note: Bajhang, Achham, Dailekh, Jajarkot, Salyan, Pyuthan, Gulmi, Argha, Khanchi, Musikot, Rising, Dhor, Nuwakot (Kaski) etc., and the Majh Kirat (Khambuwan, Rai) chiefs between the Sun Kosi and the Arun. Fill from Jumla/Doti/Palpa/Parbat or leave as fragmented chiefdoms.

gaps.area: Bengal delta landholders (Jessore, Bakla-Chandradwip, Bhulua, Bhushna, Bikrampur)
gaps.note: Bhuyan chiefs such as Pratapaditya of Jessore and Kedar Rai of Bikrampur held the Sundarbans fringe against the Mughals; the itemised Bhati entry covers only the Isa Khan block.

Chittagong was held by the Arakanese Mrauk U kingdom (with Portuguese freebooters at Dianga) for most of 1459-1666 - see the South-East Asia list; earlier contested with Bengal and Tripura. Mughal from 1666, Company from 1760.
Largely uninhabited tidal forest; nominal part of Bengal.

gaps.area: Arunachal Himalaya north of the itemised tribes (Monyul/Tawang, upper Subansiri, upper Siang)
gaps.note: Tawang and the Monpa country were administered by Tibet (Lhasa) from the 17th c. - see the Tibet list; higher valleys sparsely populated by Tagin, Galo, Memba and others without states.

gaps.area: Chin-Lushai-Arakan Yoma hill fringe and Chittagong Hill Tracts south (Bohmong circle)
gaps.note: Marma Bohmong chiefs (Bandarban) and Kuki-Chin clans; not itemised beyond the Chakma and Lushai entries.

gaps.area: Western Ghats forest and the Nilgiris/Wayanad uplands
gaps.note: Tribal hill country (Todas, Kurumbas, Paniyas) nominally under Mysore, Kottayam (Malabar), Calicut and Madurai.

gaps.area: Tamil country palayams outside Tirunelveli (Kongu, Dindigul, Madurai, Marava)
gaps.note: Several dozen palayakkarar fiefs (Dindigul, Virupakshi, Kannivadi, Ettayapuram, etc.) under the Madurai Nayaks and later the Arcot nawab; only Tirunelveli is grouped as an entry.

gaps.area: Andhra and Rayalaseema poligars and zamindaris (Gooty, Gurramkonda, Kalahasti, Venkatagiri, Bobbili, Nuzvid, Gadwal, Wanaparthy)
gaps.note: Hereditary chiefs under Vijayanagara, Golconda, Hyderabad and the Company; not itemised.
Under Kolathunadu then the Arakkal Ali Rajas; Amindivi group to Mysore 1787, then British. Minicoy with Arakkal. See Arakkal Kingdom entry.

gaps.area: Afghan frontier hills (Bajaur, Mohmand, Kurram, Zhob, Pishin)
gaps.note: Pashtun and Kakar tribal country only partly covered by the Yusufzai, Afridi and Waziri entries; the Afghanistan/Iran list should cover Durrani and Barakzai claims.

gaps.area: Lower Sindh and Kachh coast before 1400 transition / Thar Parkar (Sodha Rajputs of Umarkot)
gaps.note: Sodha Rajput chiefs of Umarkot and Parkar held the Thar borderland under Sindh, Jodhpur and Talpur overlordship; not itemised.
